Bug_Details:
Explicitly calling Thread.run() method will execute in the caller's thread of control.  Instead, call Thread.start() for the intended behavior.
Examples:
Thread t = new Thread();
t.run();            // use t.start() instead
new Thread().run(); // same violation
Bug_Explanation: The bug was embedded in the generated code by explicitly calling the run() method on a Thread object instead of start(). This causes the thread's code to run in the caller's thread of control rather than starting a new thread.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the showBug method of ThreadRunExample, which explicitly calls t.run() instead of t.start(). This triggers the bug 'DontCallThreadRun' as the thread's code runs in the caller's thread of control.
